page-05.text:
This was [Child Name]'s favorite park
in all of [Hometown].
[Child Name] ran in, ready to play.

page-06.text:
Swings. Tunnels. Sand.
A climbing wall like a mountain.

page-08.text: The slide looked even longer from here.

[Child Name] did not know 
what to do.

page-09.text:
That night, [Child Name]
sat quietly on the bed.
The big feeling was still there.
"That was scary," said a tiny voice.

page-10.text: A light blinked  beside the bed.

The lights made a path
across the floor.

"Let's look together,"
said the tiny voice.

page-11.text: "This way," said the voice. "Whenever you're ready."

page-14.text: Before [Child Name] could peek, voices called from every direction.

"This way!" blinked a star.
"No, this way!" puffed the wind.

page-15.text: And there it was: a quiet path.

page-16.text:
One way was smooth and shiny.
It looked easy.
The other was plain and steep.
[Child Name] looked at the shiny path. It was pretty.

page-17.text: At the top, a cave glittered.

page-18.text: The tiny voice echoed through the cave.
The same words glowed on a wall in big, prickly letters.
"Why do you sound mean?" asked [Child Name].

page-19.text: The voice was quiet. [Child Name] remembered.

page-20.text: "Oh. You weren't trying to be mean."
The tiny voice felt warm again.

page-21.text: "Sometimes big feelings come out sharp," said the voice.
"But if you listen close, you can hear what they are really trying to say."

page-22.text:
The prickles fell away.
The wall shimmered.
Beyond it, the world was bright.

page-24.text: "I want to see you," said [Child Name].
A trail of [animal clues] glowed ahead.
The forest grew warmer and quieter.

"Listen close," said the tiny voice.
"That quiet is your heart."

page-25.text: In a warm, magical clearing, [animal guide] appeared.
"I am your quiet voice," said [animal guide], "in a shape you can see."
The warm quiet was inside [Child Name], too.

page-26.text:
[Child Name] and [animal guide] flew through the stars.
The magical forest grew small below.
Ahead was the park, the ladder, and the very, very tall slide.

Take a slow breath in.

How does it make you feel?

Listen close. Does your quiet voice say
"no," "not yet," or "yes"?
